issue.body:
Add support for aggregation scoped filters that work dynamically on the
 data in each group.

```
| STATS
    success = COUNT(*) WHERE 200 <= code AND code < 300,
   redirect = COUNT(*) WHERE 300 <= code AND code < 400,
 client_err = COUNT(*) WHERE 400 <= code AND code < 500,
 server_err = COUNT(*) WHERE 500 <= code AND code < 600,
total_count = COUNT(*)
```

Implementation wise, the base AggregateFunction has been extended to
 allow a filter to be passed on. This is required to incorporate the
 filter as part of the aggregate equality/identify which would fail with
 the filter as an external component.

As part of the process, the serialization for the existing aggregations
 had to be fixed so AggregateFunction implementations so that it
 delegates to their parent first.

I am little confused about `run an IT ("qa") to experience the issue (like single-node)`, could you provide an example of how to execute it?

And I try another test way, I execute `./gradlew run -Dtests.es.xpack.security.enabled=false` to start local Elasticsearch in my machine and execute Reproducer step write by @alex-spies in your [cause](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/pull/113735#discussion_r1792685098)
```
POST /test/_doc?refresh'
{"a" : 1}

POST /test/_doc?refresh'
{"a" : 2}

POST /test/_doc?refresh'
{"a" : 3}

POST /test/_doc?refresh'
{"a" : 4}

POST /_query
{"query": "from test | stats sum(1) where a > 3"}
```
The query displays the result as shown below:
```
{"took":432,"columns":[{"name":"count(*) where a > 3","type":"long"}],"values":[[1]]}%
```
The query return 1 as only 1 row satisfies a > 3. Thus, I am uncertain whether it has been resolved or not.
